prompt: Marketing wants to split customers into about 5 groups by spending and visit frequency. There are no labels.
why: Unsupervised grouping into a chosen number of clusters.
trap: Classification needs labels you don't have.

prompt: Choose 8 warehouse locations so that each store is as close as possible to its nearest warehouse.
tells: close as possible to its nearest
why: Centroids minimizing distance to assigned points is exactly k-means' objective.
trap: It's geography, but the math is clustering.

prompt: Reduce a photo to its 16 most representative colors.
why: Cluster pixel colors into 16 groups; each centroid is a palette color.
trap: PCA reduces dimensions, not the number of distinct values.

prompt: Group 50,000 support tickets (already turned into embeddings) into topics nobody has defined yet.
tells: into topics nobody has defined yet
why: Cluster the embeddings and inspect each cluster to name the topics.
trap: A classifier needs predefined topics and labels.

prompt: Group 400 stores into a few types by sales mix and size, so each type gets its own strategy. Nobody has defined the types.
tells: Group 400 stores into a few types
trap: Without predefined types there's nothing to train a classifier on.

prompt: You clustered customers but don't know whether 3, 5 or 8 groups is right. The within-cluster error keeps dropping as groups are added.
why: Pick k with the elbow method or silhouette score, plus whether the segments are useful.
trap: Error always drops with more clusters, so it can't pick k on its own.

prompt: Clusters of customers form almost entirely by annual income (in dollars), ignoring visit count (0–30).
tells: almost entirely by annual income (in dollars)
why: k-means uses distances, so the large-scale feature dominates. Standardize features first.
trap: It's a k-means preprocessing issue, not a reason to change methods.

prompt: Split 20,000 delivery addresses into 12 compact zones, one per driver.
why: Cluster coordinates into 12 groups around centroids.
trap: It's geography, but the method is clustering.
